data.name: PXR (NR1I2)
data.description: Pregnane X receptor, a xenobiotic-sensing nuclear receptor. Its activation is associated with liver growth, and the AKT-mTOR pathway is the proposed route, but the evidence is male-mouse-only: no liver enlargement was seen in female mice, the 16-volunteer human arm carried no mTOR readout, and the authors' own wording is that PXR activation 'may also induce liver growth in humans' (LASSILA2026). Stated as a causal human mechanism this would be stronger than the source allows.
data.description_beginner: A sensor in liver cells that detects foreign chemicals and drugs and switches on the genes needed to break them down. Turning it on is also linked to the liver growing larger, and AKT-mTOR is the suspected route - but that was seen in male mice only, not in females, and the human part of the study never measured mTOR at all.

studies.title: Pregnane X receptor-mediated liver growth: a controlled clinical trial in healthy volunteers and identification of the role of AKT-MTOR pathway in mouse.
studies.authors: Lassila P; Karpale M; Kummu O; Stahl A; Käräjämäki A; Pääkkö E; Hammer HS; Braeuning A; Pötz O; Templin M; Hukkanen J; Hakkola J

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human controlled clinical trial (n=16); mouse (PXR-humanised, PCN)
studies.finding: One week of rifampicin increased the liver volume-to-body-weight ratio by 2.7% in 16 healthy volunteers, and PXR activation enlarged the liver in male mice, accompanied by increased AKT-MTOR pathway activity, without YAP activation.
